Apparatus criticus

  • Text checked against photograph, and as per IGPalermo

English translation

Marta Fogagnolo

Purchase of a loculus by Zosimianos.

commentary

The inscription records the purchase of a tomb by the deceased Zosimianos (the name is not attested elsewhere in Sicily, for the form Ζώσιμος, see LGPN IIIA 191). The purchase is expressed by the noun ἀγορασεία, a term attested at Catania (see IG XIV 530b, 552; SEG IV 60; Libertini 1931, 369 no. 1). The burial place was most likely a loculus, as suggested by the small dimensions of the slab, and is designated by the term ἔμβασις (for this term at Catania, see IGCVO 866; SEG XLVI 1261; IMusCatania 176; cf. Ferrua 1958, 172). Formulae expressing the purchase of a tomb by means of ἀγορασία followed by the genitive of the purchaser's — or, in funerary contexts, the deceased's — name are particularly common at Syracuse, but are also attested at Catania (SEG IV 60). In the present inscription, the genitive of the object purchased also appears, as is perhaps likewise the case in Libertini 1931, 369 no. 1 (see Korhonen 2004, 109 n. 152). The menorah engraved at the end of the inscription identifies it as belonging to the corpus of Jewish inscriptions. For the Jewish presence in Sicily, and particularly at Catania, during Late Antiquity, see Gebbia 1996.
